key_insight: Positive (nonnegative) structure adds an extra “scattering” constraint that makes tensor decompositions identifiable beyond standard dimension- and independence-based criteria.
engineering_relevance: The result gives a sharper way to certify sparse nonnegative tensor factor models, with direct implications for robust source separation, factorization, and matrix/tensor analysis.
method: Combine a positive scattering term with the Lovitz–Petrov dimension budget.
Use a positive splitting inequality for irreducible exchanges of nonnegative rank-one tensors.
Derive exact activation rules via graph connectivity, with thresholds 2|S|-2 for minimality/nonnegative rank and 2|S|-1 for uniqueness.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strict certification examples where Kruskal and Lovitz–Petrov conditions fail even after reshaping, and notes the matrix case collapses to full-rank factorization and two-sided separability.
watch_item: The scattering term is defined through an optimization over intermediate factor spaces, so practical computation and scalability may be nontrivial.
paper_title: Identifiability of Nonnegative Tensor Decompositions via Positive Scattering
